state.case_summary:
A 9-year-old boy presented with a 6-month history of swelling and moderate pain over the left clavicular area. He denied fever, weight loss, or trauma. He had received unspecified oral medications for one month at another center. His medical history was unremarkable, with no hospitalizations, chronic illnesses, or allergies. On examination, vital signs were normal. Musculoskeletal exam showed a tender 2 × 3 cm swelling over the left clavicle with a small clean overlying wound and erythema, without discharge. Shoulder range of motion was preserved, and other systems were unremarkable. Laboratory studies revealed an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 50 mm/h; complete blood count, renal and liver function tests were normal. Abdominal ultrasound was unremarkable. A chest radiograph demonstrated a midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture; the lung fields were clear.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. chronic osteomyelitis
B. Metastatic bone lesion
C. Ewing’s sarcoma
D. Congenital anomalies of the clavicle
E. Arteriovenous malformation
F. None
G. None
H. None
